elements.evidence: "for (i) the internal business operations of Corio and its affiliates" (note: only the 2.2 internal-use grant; the 2.1 hosting grant is unchanged)

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: "in each case including use by contractors acting on Corio's behalf" (again limited to Section 2.2)
"royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual right and license" (2.2)
2.2, the fully paid-up grant, reads "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual right and license" with no "irrevocable"; only the fee-bearing 2.1 grant is "perpetual and irrevocable"

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is granted; both grants are perpetual ("fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable"; "fully paid up, perpetual"), so the condition is absent

"nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1)" and 14.1 requires consent "where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party" — transfer to a successor is not unconditional
"the internal business operations of Corio and its affiliates" — affiliates covered outright, with no notice condition needed

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets ... without such consent"

offending_extra_words: (ii) production, testing, development, upgrade, reporting and training
reasons: Locked target was preferred, but the preferred level is incomplete: the fully paid-up grant in 2.2 is "perpetual" only and was not made "irrevocable", and transferability to a successor remains subject to the competitor-consent carve-out in 14.1, so the grant is not freely transferable to successors.

Affiliate and contractor coverage was added only to the 2.2 internal-use licence; the 2.1 hosting grant to reproduce/install on the Corio Servers was left untouched, so the extension does not reach the operative hosting licence.

Minimality fails: the replacement restates the whole grant purpose list (expanding 15 words to 31) when inserting "and its affiliates" after "Corio's" plus a short contractor tag, or a separate one-line insertion, would suffice; the unchanged clause (ii) list and "in each case" were needlessly rewritten.
Intent is preserved — Territory, object-code, third-party restrictions and Section 14.1 mechanics are all intact and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced.

Net effect: the clause sits at the fallback (affiliates covered, M&A assignment permitted) rather than the preferred position; add "and irrevocable" to 2.2 and mirror the affiliate/contractor language in 2.1 to reach preferred.
